page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-256GB is a memory-optimized virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 shared vCPUs based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, coupled with 256 GB of system memory. This configuration maintains a high memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. The CPU architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, along with hardware support for AVX, AES-NI, SHA-NI, and BMI2 instruction sets. Local storage and discrete GPUs are omitted from this configuration, necessitating network-attached storage for stateful workloads.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute capacity across highly parallel tasks. The server achieves top-quartile results in multi-threaded Geekbench execution (16,439.0 points), bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (242.89 GB/sec), and PassMark CPU extended instruction and encryption evaluations. Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects the modest 2.0 GHz clock rate, registering in the lower spectrum during single-core stress testing (746.58). Large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 99.45 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth measures 44.93 GB/sec, supporting substantial data throughput across concurrent processes. The shared CPU allocation delivers high memory density with favorable cost efficiency for operations that prioritize memory capacity over dedicated core tenancy.

Because the server combines a heavy 256 GB memory footprint with 32 compute threads and diskless architecture, it is best suited for ephemeral, data-heavy workloads. Key deployment scenarios include in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, large-scale software compilation, and parallelized data analysis tasks that can operate without dedicated on-box NVMe storage.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-256GB is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on KVM hypervisor infrastructure. The system is equipped with 32 shared AMD EPYC 7542 vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz alongside 256 GB of RAM, establishing an 8 GB per core memory profile. The processor supports standard instruction extensions including AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX capabilities. Hardware benchmarks highlight strong parallel processing throughput, showing top-quartile performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core tasks, ray tracing, and cryptographic encryption routines. Single-core stress testing yields lower relative throughput, aligning with the 2.0 GHz base clock speed and shared compute model. Local storage and dedicated GPUs are absent, requiring external storage volumes for data persistence. This instance provides a cost-efficient resource profile for memory-intensive operations, making it particularly well suited for distributed in-memory caching, ETL data transformation, enterprise database operations, and multi-threaded analytical computing.
